question: Take the dinosaur-killing asteroid as 10 km across, 3,000 kg/m³, at 20 km/s. Energy, in billions of Hiroshima bombs (6 × 10¹³ J each)?
move: When speed is squared, a fast small thing can outweigh a slow huge one.
trap: Reaching for millions, because no bomb scale feels big enough.
hint: Kinetic energy is half the mass times the speed squared; start with the volume.
steps: Volume: a sphere fills about half its cube, so about 520 km³, or 5.2 × 10¹¹ m³.

diagram.caption: Half the mass times the speed squared: about five billion Hiroshimas.

source: Collins et al., Meteoritics & Planetary Science, 2005
reference: Collins, Melosh & Marcus, Earth Impact Effects Program: A Web-based computer program for calculating the regional environmental consequences of a meteoroid impact on Earth, Meteoritics & Planetary Science, 2005
